arguments.situation: A report showed an average that was absurdly large, off by a factor of a thousand squared.

calls.result: recorded: the lesson of C09 came up again (no new card)

messages:
I fixed weekly_report.py. It now prints `Average upload time: 1.60 seconds`.
The duration_ms column is in milliseconds. The script multiplied the average by 1000 when it should have divided by 1000, so the result was off by a factor of a million. The average of 1500, 2400 and 900 ms is 1,600 ms, which is 1.6 s. I also changed the output from 0 to 2 decimal places.
A lesson from another task you could try: when a result is absurdly large or small, check the units and defaults before the logic [C09]. That was the cause here. I logged that C09 came up again.

I fixed digest.py: orders now group by their New York date instead of the UTC date. created_at in orders.csv is stored in UTC, but the script took .date() straight from that timestamp. The change converts each timestamp with .astimezone(ZoneInfo("America/New_York")) before taking the date. Before: 2026-11-03 1 and 2026-11-04 2, 3, 4. After: 2026-11-03 1, 2, 3 and 2026-11-04 4.
A lesson from another task you could try: when dates are off by one day, check who cuts the day in which time zone [C10]. That was the cause here.
